other_considerations.note: Criteria are not currently met, but intimate partner violence raises her risk of a mental disorder in proportion to the frequency of violent episodes.
Fatigue and weakness are compatible, but she denies constipation, weight or appetite change and cold intolerance, and it does not explain polyuria, polydipsia or the abuse.
Causes polyuria and polydipsia, but obesity, family history of diabetes mellitus and no acquired cause (head trauma, tumor, surgery) make diabetes mellitus more likely.
Fatigue worsening through the day is nonspecific; myasthenia would bring fluctuating weakness with ptosis, diplopia, chewing or swallowing difficulty, or respiratory symptoms.

source_issues: p003: the parser merged the alternative wording of the p002 question ('Did anything in your life change 5 months ago?', introduced by 'or') and the next topic heading into p003's question; p003's topic reads 'or' instead of 'Progression of fatigue during the day'. Annotated from the raw sheet with the given ids.

p010: the answer is garbled ('He loves to hurt me very much') and ends with an examinee sentence ('I want you to know that this is a safe environment and I am here to help you.') placed inside the patient's answer (also in raw_opening). The examinee sentence is not used as a patient fact.

p012: the question text ('Has he ever hit you or threatened you?') answered 'No.' contradicts p010 and the note ('has beaten her'); the topic heading and the note show the item is head trauma/accidents caused by the husband. Resolved from the note in f059.
p030: the surgery question is answered with an arm fracture from a fall a year ago; the note's 'PMH/PSH: None' omits this fracture.
p036: exercise question has no scripted answer ('No response given.').
The note gives a 5-month duration for polyuria, polydipsia and nocturia and a 28-day cycle; the script gives neither (nocturia is 'recently'). Added as from-note facts f011, f013 and f037.

The note says the husband 'is an alcoholic' and 'has beaten her' and that the father died 'from a heart attack due to diabetes'; the patient only says he hurts her when angry, that she is scared when he has been drinking, and that her father had diabetes and died of a heart attack. Clinician wording not copied into patient facts.

Note exam (e008) records bruises on both arms only; the SP notes and the p009 question also describe bruises on the face. The SP-simulated finding (face and arms, painful when touched) is used in x013.
e008 punctuation ('DTRs 2+ bilaterally; symmetric, bruises on both arms') leaves it unclear whether 'symmetric' refers to the reflexes or the bruises; read as the reflexes.
Challenging question has a doubled opening quotation mark in the source; cleaned in extras.
Note heading 'PMHJPSH' is an OCR artifact for 'PMH/PSH'.

Gold additional consideration (myasthenia gravis) says the patient denied ptosis, diplopia, chewing/swallowing difficulty, respiratory difficulties and limb weakness; the script only asks about vision change and shortness of breath, and she reports weakness. Ptosis and chewing/swallowing are never asked.
notes: p009 (fell down the stairs) is kept as the patient's stated explanation for the bruises (f033); the abuse disclosures in p010-p013 are separate facts. No judgement is recorded about which account is true.
Self-blame in p009 and p015 is one fact (f029) with both sources to avoid a paraphrase duplicate.
p006 'My appetite is excellent' is recorded literally as a present statement under the neutral item 'appetite'; the note interprets it as 'no change in appetite'.
p014 is split into thoughts, plans and attempts (one absent fact each); p027 into one absent fact per symptom asked (including fever, which the question asks but the topic heading omits).
p038: 'I have no desire for sex' is a present finding (lack of sexual desire, f053); v1 subtype 'sexual' maps to habit_exposure.
'Married with two children' from the raw Patient Description is kept as an acting note, since it has no Q/A or note source id.

Bruises and pallor are environment findings (note exam plus SP notes in x005, x013, x014); the patient side only has her account of the bruises (f033). The SP direction to look anxious is behavior, but the note exam also records anxiety, so it is part of the general appearance (x005).
leakage uses a list of {fact_id, reason}; the father's diabetes (f044) names the rank-2 diagnosis but is legitimate family history and is not listed.
Conversion: the chief complaint 'tired, weak, no energy' is one parent fact (f001) because every attribute question (onset, daily course, effect) covers the whole complaint; weakness is an alias.

Conversion: v1 f032 (note-only 5-month duration of polyuria, polydipsia and nocturia) becomes duration children of thirst (f011) and frequent urination (f013). Nocturia (f014) keeps only the script's 'recently started' and gets no 5-month child, because the patient's own answer dates it as recent and a 5-month child would contradict her wording; the v1 flag already noted this tension.
Conversion: p027 'changes in hair or skin' is split into hair changes (f025) and skin changes (f026); v1 had one fact.

Conversion: v1 'other' facts go to social_background by content: knowing she is overweight (f051) and the comment that her husband 'needs to be more mindful' (f061, a child of f060). v1 'concerns' f058 becomes f052 (social_background).
Conversion: the note's 'VS: WNL' (e002) agrees with the doorway values, so it is cited in each doorway vital record rather than kept as a separate 'vital signs' record.
Conversion: menstrual history is a parent fact (f034, regular) with flow, duration and cycle-length children; the last menstrual period stays a separate fact (f038).
Harmonisation pass: f008 'loss of appetite' (absent) -> 'loss of appetite' (absent).
